items.title: Yes, Claude can do nine loops
items.reason: Anthropic's own account of Claude computing a previously-unsolved 9-loop hexagon amplitude in N=4 super Yang-Mills, autonomously, over hours with minimal supervision.
key_facts: Previous human record was 8 loops; Claude reached 9 using two independent methods (bootstrap + form-factor).
Total cost ~$1,000-2,000; the bootstrap run alone cost ~$100 and was equivalent to 96 CPUs for a week.
Researcher gave it a 'keep working while I sleep' prompt with no further oversight for hours.
Used established physics methods via Python/SymPy rather than a novel technique.

items.title: Jevmem – automatic project memory for Claude Code, built on Jev
items.reason: A Claude Code memory plugin with real benchmark numbers, not just a pitch: cheap, fast, and includes a memory-poisoning defense.
key_facts: 98.5% accuracy on save/skip decisions across 66 held-out turns, matching GPT-6 Astra.
Runs 9-12x faster and ~40-60x cheaper than calling GPT-4/Opus directly (~$0.00013/turn, ~300ms median latency).
A poisoning-detection gate blocked 20 of 22 planted malicious memory lines in testing.
Author discloses eval sets are self-made with no independent recall-quality measurement.

No third-party benchmarks; alpha status with unstable APIs.
